subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'Subsequent records released to the operating environment have consecutively higher relative record numbers' -> OK 30)): in extend mode the first record gets highest-existing RRN + 1, later records get consecutive numbers, and the RRN is MOVEd into the RELATIVE KEY item. Code: extend mode can only be reached with ACCESS SEQUENTIAL (§14.9.27.3 SR2), and RelativeConnector.Write's sequential arm takes NextSequentialSlot() = Max(_st.Highest, _lastReleasedSlot) + 1. That is highest-existing + 1 for the first record and consecutive after it, because nothing else releases between two writes on an unshared file (GR31 covers the shared case). KeyedIoEmitter.EmitWrite then StoreArith's FileRelativeSlot into the key item when the status is successful: a MOVE-rule numeric store, with Truncation. Probe dir: out/probe/write-statement-p3/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). rel1.cob: OUTPUT writes RRN 1..3; a DYNAMIC connector adds RRN 5; OPEN EXTEND then writes 'E-OK 00 RK=6', 7, 8, 9 (consecutive, starting at highest+1), and the 5th write overflows RELATIVE KEY PIC 9 with 'E-INV 24'. The read-back walks 1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9. The test l1_open_extend_position is spec-derived: it seeds records 1 and 4 sparsely, and EXTEND gives RK=0005. It covers the first-record and MOVE sentences; the consecutive-subsequent sentence is witnessed only by the probe. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is in every edition's relative/indexed WRITE text; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to it)]
